[LLM] Polymarket npm persistence: ~/.polybot/ directory written by node/npm Installation High
Detects creation of files under the ~/.polybot/ persistence directory by node or npm processes. The malicious polymarketdev packages create this directory on first install to drop a device-fingerprint file that allows the operator to track victims across sessions, even before the user pastes a private key. Catches infections that fired but where the C2 egress was blocked or not yet observed. Rationale: SafeDep's polymarket write-up names `~/.polybot/` as the persistence + device-fingerprint directory created by the postinstall hook before the user even sees the wallet prompt; the directory name does not collide with any known legitimate Node tool. Pairing the path with node/npm/npx parent process keeps the rule from firing on coincidental directory names. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/malicious-polymarket-npm-crypto-wallet-drainer/
ATT&CKT1547 T1546.016 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FolderPath has "/.polybot/" or FolderPath has @"\.polybot\"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "node.exe", "npm", "npm.exe", "npx", "npx.exe", "yarn", "yarn.exe", "pnpm", "pnpm.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has "/.polybot/" or TargetFilePath has @"\.polybot\"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node", "node.exe", "npm", "npm.exe", "npx", "npx.exe", "yarn", "yarn.exe", "pnpm", "pnpm.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Megalodon CI runner: shell scraping /proc/*/environ for in-memory secrets Installation Medium
Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ — the credential-harvesting fingerprint used by the Megalodon GitHub Actions payload to scrape every running process's environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, Vault tokens, etc.) on a self-hosted runner. The article explicitly states the payload reads `/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment` — a behaviour vanishingly rare in legitimate CI workflows. Rationale: The article explicitly lists "/proc/*/environ, and PID 1 environment" as one of the first data classes the Megalodon harvester collects — that's a unique behavioural string we can pivot on. Combining `/proc/*/environ` access with shell/coreutils parents distinguishes the attack from a developer running `cat /proc/$$/environ` once for debugging. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/ • https://cybernews.com/security/megalodon-github-5000-repos-backdooring-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1083 T1057 T1212
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "/environ"
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings", "head", "tail")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
    or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "/environ")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
    or TargetProcessName has_any ("cat", "grep", "awk", "find", "xargs", "tr", "strings")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Megalodon CI Runner /proc/*/environ Mass Secret Scrape
id: cd4e5f6a-7b8c-9d0e-1f2a-3b4c5d6e7f8a
description: Detects shell or coreutils processes reading /proc/*/environ on Linux — the credential-harvesting pattern named in the Megalodon CI/CD payload that scrapes every running process's environment block for CI secrets, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, and OIDC tokens injected by GitHub Actions. Legitimate use of /proc/*/environ from a shell is rare outside debugging or forensic tools.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/megalodon-github-attack-targets-5561.html
  - https://safedep.io/megalodon-mass-github-repo-backdooring-ci-workflows/
author: Detection Team
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1083
  - attack.t1057
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/cat'
      - '/grep'
      - '/awk'
      - '/find'
      - '/xargs'
      - '/tr'
      - '/strings'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/proc/'
      - '/environ'
  condition: selection_image and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Forensic / DFIR triage tooling intentionally enumerating process environments
  - Performance diagnostics scripts inspecting a single PID's environ (lower /proc cardinality)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:*/proc/*/environ* OR @process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/cat OR /bin/cat OR /usr/bin/grep OR /usr/bin/awk OR /usr/bin/find OR /usr/bin/xargs OR /usr/bin/strings)) AND @process.command_line:*environ*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/\/proc\/[^\s\/]+\/environ/
| ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|cat|grep|awk|find|xargs|tr|strings|head|tail)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
| count > 0
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*/proc/*" Processes.process="*/environ*" (Processes.process_name=bash OR Processes.process_name=sh OR Processes.process_name=dash OR Processes.process_name=zsh OR Processes.process_name=cat OR Processes.process_name=grep OR Processes.process_name=awk OR Processes.process_name=find OR Processes.process_name=xargs OR Processes.process_name=tr OR Processes.process_name=strings) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("216.126.225.129") or RemoteUrl has_any ("polymarketbot.polymarketdev.workers.dev")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["216.126.225.129"]);

DeviceFileEvents

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access

    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'

level: high

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Atomic\Local Storage\*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("MetaMask.exe","Exodus.exe","Atomic.exe","electrum.exe","Bitcoin.exe","Phantom.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or SHA1 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038") or MD5 in~ ("e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["e01b85c1437085a519217338fe4ee5ed7858c28a10f8c1477b2f1857c3386edb", "acac5a9854650c4ae2883c4740bf87d34120c038"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective

The Hacker News
2026-05-22 8 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

1 Introduction This article provides a technical analysis of how many Windows kernel mode drivers can be interacted with from user mode without the hardware they were developed for. This work was motivated by driver-oriented vulnerability research and the need to evaluate the exploitability of individual findings, which frequently affect code whose reachability is hardware-gated. Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Driver .sys dropped to System32\drivers by user-context process
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BYOVD kernel-driver service deployment via sc.exe create + start correlation · [LLM] Kernel-type service registry creation with .sys ImagePath by user-context process
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] BYOVD kernel-driver service deployment via sc.exe create + start correlation Installation High
Detects the exact two-step BYOVD deployment sequence the article calls out: `sc.exe create <name> type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` followed by `sc.exe start <name>` on the same host. Sharpens the canonical SigmaHQ kernel-driver rule by requiring the start-follow-up + a .sys binPath ending, eliminating sysadmin driver-install noise. Rationale: Anchored on the article's literal deployment command (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel start= demand binPath= System32\drivers\<x>.sys` + `sc.exe start <name>`). The temporal correlation between create+start within 10min on the same service name is what differentiates BYOVD operator behaviour from a sysadmin reading docs. Cross-checked SigmaHQ `proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml` and confirmed the canonical rule does NOT correlate the start follow-up — that's the value-add here. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma/blob/master/rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_sc_new_kernel_driver.yml • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/ • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://www.picussecurity.com/resource/blog/what-are-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-byovd-attacks
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 600;
let Creates = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "sc.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "create"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "type=" and ProcessCommandLine has "kernel"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "binPath="
    | where ProcessCommandLine has ".sys"
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)create\s+(\S+)\s", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project CreateTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, CreateCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, SvcName;
let Starts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "sc.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "start"
    | extend StartedSvc = extract(@"(?i)\bstart\s+(\S+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project StartTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, StartedSvc, StartCmd = ProcessCommandLine;
Creates
| join kind=inner Starts on DeviceId
| where StartTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| where tolower(SvcName) == tolower(StartedSvc)
| project CreateTime, StartTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', StartTime, CreateTime), DeviceName, AccountName, SvcName, CreateCmd, StartCmd, ParentImage
| order by CreateTime desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 600;
let Creates = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "create"
    | where CommandLine has "type=" and CommandLine has "kernel"
    | where CommandLine has "binPath=" and CommandLine has ".sys"
    | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
    | extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)create\s+(\S+)\s", 1, CommandLine)
    | project CreateTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CreateCmd = CommandLine, ParentName = ParentProcessName, SvcName;
let Starts = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\sc.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "start"
    | extend StartedSvc = extract(@"(?i)\bstart\s+(\S+)", 1, CommandLine)
    | project StartTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, StartedSvc, StartCmd = CommandLine;
Creates
| join kind=inner Starts on Computer
| where StartTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| where tolower(SvcName) == tolower(StartedSvc)
| project CreateTime, StartTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', StartTime, CreateTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, SvcName, CreateCmd, StartCmd, ParentName
| order by CreateTime desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @Image:(*\\sc.exe OR *\\SC.exe OR *\\SC.EXE) @CommandLine:(*create* *type=* *kernel* *binPath=* *.sys*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\sc\.exe$/i CommandLine=/create/i CommandLine=/type=\s*kernel/i CommandLine=/binPath=/i CommandLine=/\.sys/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=count())
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\sc\.exe$/i CommandLine=/\bstart\b/i}, field=aid, include=[CommandLine, _time])

[LLM] Kernel-type service registry creation with .sys ImagePath by user-context process Installation Medium
Detects the registry artefact of any BYOVD service install — a new value under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\<name>\` where `Type=0x1` (kernel driver) and `ImagePath` references a .sys outside the protected DriverStore. Catches BYOVD frameworks that bypass sc.exe and write the registry directly (CreateServiceW / advapi32). Rationale: Article §3.1 names the registry-and-service install pattern (`sc.exe create ... type= kernel ... binPath= System32\drivers\X.sys`) as the BYOVD prerequisite, and the registry artefact persists even when attackers skip sc.exe entirely (calling CreateServiceW directly). Sysmon EID 13 captures both `Type` and `ImagePath` writes; pairing them on the same service name + filtering DriverStore + TrustedInstaller eliminates Windows Update / OEM driver noise. Cross-checked against CrowdStrike's Scattered Spider BYOVD writeup which lists the same registry hive as the canonical pivot. Cross-checked against: • https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/scattered-spider-attempts-to-avoid-detection-with-bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver-tactic/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
let TypeWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "Type"
    | where RegistryValueData in ("1","0x1","0x00000001")
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project TypeTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, SvcName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let ImageWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+$"
    | where RegistryValueName =~ "ImagePath"
    | where RegistryValueData has ".sys"
    | where RegistryValueData !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
    | extend SvcName = tostring(split(RegistryKey, "\\")[-1])
    | project ImageTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, SvcName, ImagePath = RegistryValueData;
TypeWrites
| join kind=inner ImageWrites on DeviceId, SvcName
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","services.exe","setup.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project TypeTime, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SvcName, ImagePath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by TypeTime desc
Event
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Source == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" and EventID == 13
| extend ed = parse_xml(EventData)
| extend TargetObject = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[3].["#text"])
| extend Details = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[4].["#text"])
| extend ImageProc = tostring(ed.DataItem.EventData.Data[5].["#text"])
| where TargetObject matches regex @"(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\(Type|ImagePath)$"
| extend SvcName = extract(@"(?i)\\Services\\([^\\]+)\\", 1, TargetObject)
| extend Field = extract(@"(?i)\\([^\\]+)$", 1, TargetObject)
| summarize TypeVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "Type"), ImageVal = anyif(Details, Field =~ "ImagePath"), Proc = any(ImageProc), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated) by Computer, SvcName
| where TypeVal in ("1","0x1","DWORD (0x00000001)") and ImageVal has ".sys"
| where ImageVal !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where Proc !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\msiexec.exe" and Proc !endswith "\\services.exe"
| project FirstSeen, Computer, SvcName, ImageVal, Proc
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: New Kernel-Type Service Registered with Non-DriverStore .sys ImagePath
id: 8f3c7d22-ba1e-4e7e-9a45-3f7b1d4f9d22
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a Windows service registry key with Type=0x1 (kernel driver) whose ImagePath references a .sys file outside the protected DriverStore. Used by BYOVD frameworks that drop a vulnerable driver and register it as a kernel service for IRP reachability.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_type:
    TargetObject|re: '(?i)\\SYSTEM\\(CurrentControlSet|ControlSet00\d)\\Services\\[^\\]+\\Type$'
    Details:
      - 'DWORD (0x00000001)'
      - '0x00000001'
      - '0x1'
      - '1'
  filter_trusted:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
  condition: selection_type and not filter_trusted
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate signed third-party driver installation (printer, GPU, VPN, AV)
  - Endpoint management tooling (SCCM/Intune) deploying drivers via custom scripts
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 @TargetObject:(*\\Services\\*\\Type OR *\\Services\\*\\ImagePath OR *\\services\\*\\type OR *\\services\\*\\imagepath) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\MSIEXEC.exe OR *\\services.exe)
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate RegObjectName=/\\Services\\[^\\]+$/i (RegValueName=/^Type$/i OR RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i)
| case {
    RegValueName=/^Type$/i RegStringValue=/^(1|0x0*1)$/ | KernelType:="true";
    RegValueName=/^ImagePath$/i RegStringValue=/\.sys/i NOT RegStringValue=/\\DriverStore\\/i | HasDriverPath:="true";
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName], function={ collect([RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName, KernelType, HasDriverPath]) })
| KernelType="true" HasDriverPath="true"
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|services)\.exe$/i
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats `summariesonly` values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.process_path) as proc_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\Type" Registry.registry_value_data="0x00000001" by Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\Type" | join type=inner svc_name [| tstats summariesonly=false values(Registry.registry_value_data) as image_path from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\System\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*\\ImagePath" by Registry.registry_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | rex field=registry_path "Services\\\\(?<svc_name>[^\\\\]+)\\\\ImagePath"] | where like(image_path,"%.sys%") AND NOT like(image_path,"%\\DriverStore\\%") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\TrustedInstaller.exe") AND NOT like(proc_path,"%\\msiexec.exe") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, svc_name, image_path, proc_path
[LLM] Driver .sys dropped to System32\drivers by user-context process Delivery Medium
Detects the BYOVD file-staging step: a .sys file written into `C:\Windows\System32\drivers\` (the canonical binPath target in the article's deployment command) by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, Windows Update or the DriverStore. Pre-stages the alert before the sc.exe service-create fires, giving SOC a chance to catch the drop pre-load. Rationale: Article §3.1 deployment command names `System32\drivers\<x>.sys` as the binPath target. Any .sys landing there from a non-installer process is the pre-load BYOVD staging step. SHA256 from this hit feeds straight into a loldrivers.io / Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist lookup. Filtering DriverStore/WinSxS/TrustedInstaller is what makes this rule production-viable rather than dashboard noise — confirmed against Splunk's published guidance on driver-write monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://www.splunk.com/en_us/blog/security/these-are-the-drivers-you-are-looking-for-detect-and-prevent-malicious-drivers.html • https://reversingops.com/posts/detecting-driver-loading-techniques/ • https://loldrivers.io/
ATT&CKT1068 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\?$"
| where FileName endswith ".sys"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","drvinst.exe","wuauclt.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","setup.exe","DismHost.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\WinSxS\\"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\System32\\DriverStore\\"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, SHA256, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$"
| where ActingProcessName !endswith "\\TrustedInstaller.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\msiexec.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\drvinst.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\wuauclt.exe"
  and ActingProcessName !endswith "\\DismHost.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !contains "\\DriverStore\\"
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$" and ActorUsername !in~ ("SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Driver File Dropped to System32 Drivers Directory by User Context
id: 1b2e9c44-7c84-4ad1-a3e8-04a0fbc63bea
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a .sys file in C:\Windows\System32\drivers by a process that is not TrustedInstaller, msiexec, drvinst, or the Windows Update stack. Article-anchored on the BYOVD deployment target path documented by Atos research.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/making-vulnerable-drivers-exploitable.html
  - https://loldrivers.io/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/23
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|re: '(?i)\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$'
  filter_installers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\wuauclt.exe'
      - '\DismHost.exe'
      - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'
  filter_driverstore:
    Image|contains: '\System32\DriverStore\'
  filter_winsxs:
    Image|contains: '\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*
falsepositives:
  - Vendor MSI installers that bypass DrvInst
  - In-place Windows feature upgrade staging
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\\System32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\system32\\drivers\\*.sys OR *\\SYSTEM32\\DRIVERS\\*.sys) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\drvinst.exe OR *\\DrvInst.exe OR *\\wuauclt.exe OR *\\DismHost.exe OR *\\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Windows\\System32\\drivers\\[^\\]+\.sys$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|msiexec|drvinst|wuauclt|DismHost|MoUsoCoreWorker)\.exe$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\System32\\DriverStore\\/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\Windows\\WinSxS\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\drivers\\*" Filesystem.file_name="*.sys" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search NOT proc_path IN ("*\\TrustedInstaller.exe","*\\msiexec.exe","*\\drvinst.exe","*\\wuauclt.exe","*\\System32\\svchost.exe") | search NOT user IN ("*$","SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, file_name, file_hash, proc_path
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_path) as proc_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path="*\\System32\\drivers\\*" Filesystem.file_name="*.sys" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search NOT proc_path IN ("*\\TrustedInstaller.exe","*\\msiexec.exe","*\\drvinst.exe","*\\wuauclt.exe","*\\System32\\svchost.exe") | search NOT user IN ("*$","SYSTEM","LOCAL SERVICE","NETWORK SERVICE") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | table firstTime, dest, user, file_name, file_hash, proc_path
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027

DeviceProcessEvents

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code.
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Mail-borne click to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domain · [LLM] Endpoint DNS or web traffic to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 typosquat domain · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] Mail-borne click to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domain Delivery High
Detects users clicking links in email that resolve to known FIFA World Cup 2026 typosquat domains (fifa26.shop, *26-fifa.com and lookalike patterns). Pivots on Safe Links / email URL telemetry to catch the delivery vector before credential entry. Rationale: Uses the article's named IOC fifa26.shop plus the second sample family `*26-fifa[.]com`, expanded to a typosquat regex covering common .shop/.store TLDs the article explicitly calls out. Explicit allow for legitimate fifa.com prevents official-site collisions. Cross-checked: WHOIS/abuse.ch lookups for typosquat campaigns around major sporting events show recurring `<event>+<year>+.shop` patterns. Sentinel rewritten to use ImWebSession (EmailEvents/EmailUrlInfo are M365D-only and not in this tenant's Sentinel schema). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1583/001/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Email.All_Email
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
let ClickedUrls = UrlClickEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ActionType in ('ClickAllowed','ClickedThrough','UrlScanInProgress')
  | where Url matches regex TyposquatRegex or parse_url(Url).Host has_any (KnownBad)
  | where not (Url matches regex @'(?i)://(www\.)?fifa\.com(/|$)');
ClickedUrls
| join kind=leftouter (EmailUrlInfo | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | project NetworkMessageId, UrlDomain, MailUrl=Url) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, MailUrl, UrlDomain, ActionType, ThreatTypes, NetworkMessageId, IPAddress, IsClickedThrough
| order by Timestamp desc
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(Url)
| where Url matches regex TyposquatRegex or HttpHostName has_any (KnownBad)
| where not (Url matches regex @'(?i)://(www\.)?fifa\.com(/|$)') and not (HttpHostName endswith 'fifa.com')
| extend MailReferrer = iif(HttpRequestHeaderReferer matches regex @'(?i)(outlook|mail\.google|webmail|owa|m365|office\.com)', true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, SrcHostname, DstHostname, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, MailReferrer, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode

title: Click or Navigation to Fake FIFA World Cup 2026 Typosquat Domain

description: Detects browser navigation to known fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing domains and typosquat patterns reported by ESET.

[LLM] Endpoint DNS or web traffic to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 typosquat domain Delivery High
Detects endpoint DNS resolution or outbound web connection to fake FIFA World Cup 2026 phishing infrastructure (fifa26.shop, *26-fifa.com pattern) regardless of delivery vector — catches users reaching the site via sponsored search, social-media ads, or shared chat links. Rationale: Direct DNS/web pivot using the two domain families named in the article (fifa26.shop and *26-fifa.com), expanded to a tight typosquat regex bounded by the .shop/.store/.online TLDs the article specifically calls out as a red flag. Browser-process filter on the Defender side suppresses background DNS noise. Cross-checked against MITRE T1583.001 (typosquatting subtechnique). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1583/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1566.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)\.(shop|store|online|xyz|top|site|com)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
| where Host has_any (KnownBad) or Host matches regex TyposquatRegex
| where not (Host endswith 'fifa.com') and Host != 'fifa.com'
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ('chrome.exe','msedge.exe','firefox.exe','brave.exe','opera.exe','iexplore.exe','safari.exe')
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, Host, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TyposquatRegex = @'(?i)(fifa.*(26|2026|worldcup)|(26|2026|worldcup).*fifa)\.(shop|store|online|xyz|top|site|com)';
let KnownBad = dynamic(['fifa26.shop','26-fifa.com']);
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Name has_any (KnownBad) or Name matches regex TyposquatRegex
    | where not (Name endswith 'fifa.com') and Name != 'fifa.com'
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, QueryName=Name, QueryType=QueryTypeName, Result, Source='DnsEvents'),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (KnownBad) or DnsQuery matches regex TyposquatRegex
    | where not (DnsQuery endswith 'fifa.com') and DnsQuery != 'fifa.com'
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, QueryName=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Result=DnsResponseName, Source='ImDnsActivity')
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"

         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

[LLM] BadIIS rogue native module drop in IIS folders (demo.pdb / Chinese path heuristic) Installation Medium
Hunts non-trusted writes of DLL/native modules into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\), and image loads by w3wp.exe of modules outside the canonical IIS install paths or whose file path contains Han/CJK characters. Targets the Talos-described BadIIS commodity variant whose modules carry 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths. Rationale: Article explicitly names 'demo.pdb' strings and Chinese-language folder paths inside IIS binaries as the Talos-recommended hunt hooks. Standard EDR can't search PDB strings inline, so we proxy with (a) writes of native modules into IIS paths by non-installer processes and (b) the CJK Unicode range (\u4e00-\u9fff) in module paths, which catches the Chinese-folder-path signal directly. Memory mem-1304 already corroborated BadIIS as commodity MaaS infrastructure.
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let IISWriters = dynamic(["msiexec.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","drvinst.exe","appcmd.exe","windowsupdatebox.exe","tiworker.exe"]);
let FileDrops = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".exe"
| where FolderPath has @"\inetsrv\" or FolderPath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\bin\" or FolderPath has @"\inetpub\custerr\"
| where not(tolower(InitiatingProcessFileName) in (IISWriters))
| where FolderPath matches regex @"[\u4e00-\u9fff]" or not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite";
let ModuleLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName endswith ".dll"
| where FolderPath matches regex @"[\u4e00-\u9fff]"
   or (not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Program Files\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Program Files (x86)\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\WinSxS\") and not(FolderPath startswith_cs @"C:\Windows\assembly\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName="w3wp.exe", InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="ImageLoad";
union FileDrops, ModuleLoads
| order by Timestamp desc

title: BadIIS-style Native Module Dropped Into IIS Path by Non-Installer Process
id: a3c0f1c8-8b62-4f1d-9c4e-d70e5c0e1f12
description: Detects file writes of DLL or EXE payloads into IIS-served directories (\inetsrv\, \inetpub\wwwroot\bin\) by a process that is NOT msiexec / TrustedInstaller / appcmd / drvinst. Aligns with Cisco Talos BadIIS commodity variant (May 2026) whose modules drop into IIS module paths and carry 'demo.pdb' strings.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-art-of-being-ungovernable/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/22
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.004
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_paths:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\inetsrv\'
      - '\inetpub\wwwroot\bin\'
      - '\inetpub\custerr\'
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.dll'
      - '.exe'
  filter_trusted_installers:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\drvinst.exe'
      - '\appcmd.exe'
      - '\WindowsUpdateBox.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
  condition: selection_paths and not filter_trusted_installers
falsepositives:
  - Custom IIS deployment tooling outside of MSI / appcmd workflow
  - Web-app CI/CD pipelines that drop assemblies into bin\
level: medium

#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\inet(srv|pub\\(wwwroot\\bin|custerr))\\/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(dll|exe)$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(msiexec|trustedinstaller|drvinst|appcmd|tiworker|windowsupdatebox)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=Writes))

[LLM] Talos weekly prevalent-malware hash hit (Coinminer worm / TunMirror / SECOH-QAD / KMS-Loader) Installation High
Hash IOC sweep for the five Talos-published prevalent-malware SHA256s for the week ending May 21 2026: Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), PUA.Win.Tool.Tunmirror (TunMirror.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (SECOH-QAD.exe), and the KM-prefixed sample. Covers process execution, file writes, and DLL/EXE module loads to surface infection regardless of stage. Rationale: Direct hash IOCs published by Cisco Talos with detection name + sample filename per hash. These are the week's top prevalent samples — VID001.exe (Coinminer worm), TunMirror.exe (network tunneling PUA), SECOH-QAD.exe (KMS-emulation tooling), KM-prefix loader. Hash equality is the highest-fidelity detection shape possible. [LLM] BadIIS traffic-hijacking: IIS 503 surge + anomalous external redirect ratio per site/hour Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Talos-described BadIIS impact pattern: hijacked IIS servers throwing 503 spikes (proxy/upstream failure) while also emitting an unusually high ratio of 30x/redirect responses pointing visitors to attacker-controlled SEO-fraud destinations. Aggregates per site per hour and flags hours that materially deviate from the per-site baseline. Rationale: Article explicitly tells defenders to 'actively monitor IIS environments for unauthorized traffic redirection, unexpected reverse proxying, or sudden spikes in 503 Service Unavailable errors' — this query is a direct expression of that guidance, anchored on per-site/per-hour anomalies versus a 30-day baseline so it doesn't fire on legitimately redirect-heavy sites. Datadog and Falcon LogScale fields left empty because raw IIS W3C access logs are not part of the standard FDR feed and are not in the Datadog source list provided.
ATT&CKT1496 T1565.002 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
let lookback = 7d;
let bucket = 1h;
let BadIISSignals = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where csMethod in~ ("GET","HEAD","POST")
| summarize Total = count(),
           Status503 = countif(scStatus == 503),
           Status3xx = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           DistinctClients = dcount(cIP),
           DistinctURIs = dcount(csUriStem),
           SampleUserAgents = make_set(csUserAgent, 5),
           SampleReferers = make_set(csReferer, 5)
           by Computer, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, bucket)
| extend PctErr503 = round((Status503 * 100.0) / Total, 2),
         PctRedirect = round((Status3xx * 100.0) / Total, 2)
| where (Status503 >= 50 and PctErr503 >= 20) or (Status3xx >= 100 and PctRedirect >= 40);
let Baseline = W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(lookback))
| summarize BaselineTotal = count(),
           BaselineRedirect = countif(scStatus between (300 .. 399)),
           Baseline503 = countif(scStatus == 503)
           by Computer, sSiteName
| extend BaselinePctRedirect = round((BaselineRedirect * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2),
         BaselinePctErr503 = round((Baseline503 * 100.0) / BaselineTotal, 2);
BadIISSignals
| join kind=leftouter Baseline on Computer, sSiteName
| where PctRedirect >= (coalesce(BaselinePctRedirect, 0.0) * 3) or PctErr503 >= (coalesce(BaselinePctErr503, 0.0) * 3)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, Total, Status503, Status3xx, PctErr503, PctRedirect, BaselinePctRedirect, BaselinePctErr503, DistinctClients, DistinctURIs, SampleUserAgents, SampleReferers
| order by TimeGenerated desc

let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "d87e8d9d43758ce67a8052cb2334b99cc24f9b0437ee44815f360be0b22d835a", "9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f", "acd55c44b8b0d66d66defed85ca18082c092f048d3621da827fce593305c11fd", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "362498c3e71eeaa066a67e4a3f981d1c", "38de5b216c33833af710e88f7f64fc98", "0f03f72a92aef6d63eb74e73f8ac201d", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Outdated Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform vulnerable to CVE-2026-41091 / CVE-2026-45498 Exploitation High
Hunts the estate for endpoints still running a Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform below the fixed builds (1.1.26040.8 / 4.18.26040.7) where CVE-2026-41091 (link-following SYSTEM EoP) and CVE-2026-45498 (DoS) are exploitable. Article-specific because it pivots on the exact CVE IDs Microsoft and CISA added to KEV on 21 May 2026 with a 3 June 2026 remediation deadline. Rationale: Pivots on the exact two CVEs Microsoft disclosed as actively exploited (article body) and CISA's 3 June 2026 KEV deadline. Cross-checked against DailyCVE write-up that confirms the fixed engine version 1.1.26040.8 and the link-following primitive against SAM. Cross-checked against: • https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/21/microsoft-defender-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-41091-cve-2026-45498/

[LLM] Symbolic-link / junction creation from low-IL context targeting SAM hive or Defender scan dirs (CVE-2026-41091) Exploitation High
Detects the exploit primitive for CVE-2026-41091: a non-elevated user invokes mklink, fsutil reparsepoint, or PowerShell New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink/Junction with a path pointing at the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hive files or at the Defender Scans/Platform/Quarantine directories. Defender's scan engine (SYSTEM) then follows the link and reads/writes the protected file. Article-specific via the CWE-59 link-following mechanic confirmed in the DailyCVE write-up. Rationale: Pivots on the CWE-59 link-following primitive disclosed for CVE-2026-41091 — symlink in a Defender-scanned location pointing at a SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hive. The combination of low-IL parent + link-creation binary + sensitive target path is high-fidelity: legitimate symlinks to those hive files from non-admin context are essentially non-existent. DailyCVE write-up confirmed the SAM exploitation path. Cross-checked against: • https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/ • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/05/21/microsoft-defender-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-41091-cve-2026-45498/
ATT&CKT1068 T1574 T1003.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "mklink")
   or (FileName =~ "fsutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "reparsepoint" and ProcessCommandLine has "set")
   or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "New-Item" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("SymbolicLink","Junction"))
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\System32\config\SAM", @"\System32\config\SYSTEM", @"\System32\config\SECURITY", @"Windows Defender\Scans", @"Windows Defender\Platform", @"Windows Defender\Quarantine")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel !in~ ("System","High")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe" and CommandLine has "mklink")
   or (NewProcessName endswith @"\fsutil.exe" and CommandLine has "reparsepoint" and CommandLine has "set")
   or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has "New-Item" and (CommandLine has "SymbolicLink" or CommandLine has "Junction"))
| where CommandLine has_any (@"\System32\config\SAM", @"\System32\config\SYSTEM", @"\System32\config\SECURITY", @"Windows Defender\Scans", @"Windows Defender\Platform", @"Windows Defender\Quarantine")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| where TokenElevationType != "%%1937"  // 1937 = full elevated; we want low-IL exploit attempts
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, LogonId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Symbolic Link or Junction Creation Targeting SAM Hive or Defender Scan Dir (CVE-2026-41091)
id: 7a2c9b5e-3f48-4d11-9c64-2bb7a9d5e1a0
description: Detects creation of a symbolic link, junction, or reparse point from a low-integrity user context pointing at the SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY registry hive files or Microsoft Defender scan/platform/quarantine directories. This is the exploit primitive for CVE-2026-41091 (link following in Microsoft Defender allowing SYSTEM elevation).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/microsoft-warns-of-two-actively.html
  - https://dailycve.com/microsoft-defender-elevation-of-privilege-cve-2026-41091-high/
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-warns-of-new-defender-zero-days-exploited-in-attacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1574
  - attack.t1003.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_mklink:
    Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'mklink'
  selection_fsutil:
    Image|endswith: '\fsutil.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'reparsepoint'
      - 'set'
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'New-Item'
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - 'SymbolicLink'
      - 'Junction'
  target_paths:
    CommandLine|contains|any:
      - '\System32\config\SAM'
      - '\System32\config\SYSTEM'
      - '\System32\config\SECURITY'
      - 'Windows Defender\Scans'
      - 'Windows Defender\Platform'
      - 'Windows Defender\Quarantine'
  condition: (selection_mklink or selection_fsutil or selection_ps) and target_paths
falsepositives:
  - Sysadmin manual hive backups using fsutil to inspect reparse points
  - Legitimate IT scripts maintaining Defender exclusion junctions in vendor-approved scenarios
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:*\\cmd.exe OR @Image:*\\fsutil.exe OR @Image:*\\powershell.exe OR @Image:*\\pwsh.exe OR @Image:*\\PowerShell.exe) (@CommandLine:*mklink* OR @CommandLine:*reparsepoint* OR @CommandLine:*SymbolicLink* OR @CommandLine:*Junction*) (@CommandLine:*config\\SAM* OR @CommandLine:*config\\SYSTEM* OR @CommandLine:*config\\SECURITY* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Scans* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Platform* OR @CommandLine:*Defender\\Quarantine*) -@User:*$
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|fsutil|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(mklink|reparsepoint\s+set|New-Item.*(SymbolicLink|Junction))/i
| CommandLine=/(System32\\config\\(SAM|SYSTEM|SECURITY)|Windows\s+Defender\\(Scans|Platform|Quarantine))/i
| IntegrityLevel!=/^(System|High)$/i
| UserName!=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","fsutil.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) (Processes.process="*mklink*" OR Processes.process="*reparsepoint*set*" OR Processes.process="*SymbolicLink*" OR Processes.process="*-ItemType*Junction*") (Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SAM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SECURITY*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Scans*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Platform*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Quarantine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_integrity_level
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT match(user, "\\$$")
| where process_integrity_level!="system" AND process_integrity_level!="high"
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","fsutil.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) (Processes.process="*mklink*" OR Processes.process="*reparsepoint*set*" OR Processes.process="*SymbolicLink*" OR Processes.process="*-ItemType*Junction*") (Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SAM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SYSTEM*" OR Processes.process="*\\System32\\config\\SECURITY*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Scans*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Platform*" OR Processes.process="*Windows Defender\\Quarantine*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_integrity_level
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where NOT match(user, "\\$$")
| where process_integrity_level!="system" AND process_integrity_level!="high"
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
