File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or SHA1 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9") or MD5 in~ ("CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["CB4E50433336707381429707F59C3CBE8D497D98", "1DF40A4A31B30B62EC33DC6FECC2C4408302ADC7", "7DCFE9EE25841DFD58D3D6871BF867FE32141DFB", "77F1970D620216C5FFF4E14A6CCC13FCCC267217", "948159A7FC2E688386864BEA59FD40DFFC4B24D6", "A3C077BDF8898E612CCD65BC82E7960834ADB2A9"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) · [LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Compromised Microsoft durabletask PyPI Package Install (TeamPCP 1.4.1-1.4.3) Delivery High
Detects pip/python installing the TeamPCP-compromised durabletask versions (1.4.0-1.4.3) — Microsoft's Durable Task Python SDK was published with a malicious dropper that fetches rope.pyz. Article-specific because it pins the exact package + version range named in the campaign. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package name 'durabletask' and version range from the article's code blocks plus external corroboration (Wiz, safedep, Aikido confirmed 1.4.1-1.4.3 as the malicious versions published 2026-05-19). pip+package-name+specific-version is high-fidelity — there is no legitimate reason to pin those exact malicious versions. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/microsofts-durabletask-pypi-package-compromised-in-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
    or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "durabletask" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("pip","pip3","python","python3")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "durabletask"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("1.4.1","1.4.2","1.4.3","==1.4.")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Fetch from check.git-service.com C2 Command & Control High
Detects DNS, HTTP, or direct-IP egress to the TeamPCP C2 infrastructure that hosts the durabletask second-stage dropper (rope.pyz). Article-specific because it pins the exact filename and the campaign's named C2 domains. Rationale: Uses the exact payload filename 'rope.pyz' from article code-block 3 and the campaign C2 domain check.git-service.com confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido. No legitimate developer infrastructure resolves these domains — they were registered 2026-05-16 by the actor and have no clean use case. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-investigating-teampcp-claimed.html

[LLM] TeamPCP rope.pyz Dropper Infection Markers on Linux Installation High
Detects creation of TeamPCP's on-disk artifacts from the durabletask compromise: the rope.pyz / managed.pyz dropper payloads in /tmp/ and the ~/.cache/.sys-update-check infection marker. Article-specific because rope.pyz is named verbatim in code block 3. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim 'rope.pyz' filename from article code block 3, plus the marker files /tmp/managed.pyz and ~/.cache/.sys-update-check confirmed by Wiz, safedep, and Aikido as the dropper's on-disk artifacts. None of these paths/filenames have legitimate Linux usage — they are unique to this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/durabletask-package-compromised-mini-shai-hulud
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/" and (FileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or FileName =~ "rope.pyz" or FileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (FolderPath has "/.cache/" and FileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/" and (TargetFileName matches regex @"^rope-.+\.pyz$" or TargetFileName =~ "rope.pyz" or TargetFileName =~ "managed.pyz"))
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.cache/" and TargetFileName in~ (".sys-update-check",".sys-update-check-k8s"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] AWS SSM SendCommand Fan-out from EC2 Instance Role (TeamPCP Worm Propagation) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the durabletask worm's lateral-movement stage: a single EC2-instance IAM role calling ssm:SendCommand against multiple EC2 instances within a short window. The rope.pyz worm uses stolen instance-role credentials to push itself to peer instances via SSM RunCommand. Rationale: Captures the worm's worm-stage primitive (ssm:SendCommand from an instance role to peer instances) which Wiz and safedep flagged as the AWS-specific propagation method. CloudTrail-only — Defender XDR and Falcon FDR don't ingest AWS control-plane events, hence empty defender_kql / falcon_logscale_query. Sentinel has the AWSCloudTrail connector but the table isn't in our canonical schema, so left empty rather than guess column names. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1651 T1078.004
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
source:cloudtrail @evt.name:SendCommand @userIdentity.type:AssumedRole @requestParameters.instanceIds:* (-@userAgent:(*aws-cli/* AND *root/*) AND -@userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName:(*ssm-automation* OR *patch-manager* OR *config-rule*))
CLOUD
`cloudtrail` eventName=SendCommand eventSource="ssm.amazonaws.com" "userIdentity.type"="AssumedRole" 
| eval source_role=mvindex(split('userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.arn',"/"),-1)
| eval target_count=mvcount('requestParameters.instanceIds{}')
| stats latest(_time) as last_seen dc('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as DistinctTargets values('requestParameters.instanceIds{}') as Targets values(sourceIPAddress) as SourceIPs values(userAgent) as UAs by source_role 'userIdentity.arn' awsRegion
| where DistinctTargets >= 3 OR like(source_role, "%ec2%") OR like(source_role, "%-instance-%")
| sort 0 -last_seen
[LLM] Python Process Reading Multi-Cloud Credential Stores (durabletask Stealer Stage) Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects a single Python process opening credential files from THREE OR MORE distinct cloud/dev ecosystems within a 5-minute window — the signature behaviour of the rope.pyz multi-cloud stealer that harvests AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, GitHub, Docker, and SSH secrets in one pass. Rationale: Targets the rope.pyz second-stage behaviour that Wiz and safedep documented: a single python process enumerating credentials across AWS + Azure + GCP + Kubernetes + npm + GitHub + Docker + SSH within seconds. The DistinctSecretFamilies>=3 threshold eliminates legitimate cloud SDKs that touch one ecosystem at a time while still catching the multi-cloud stealer in a single hit. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/durabletask-teampcp-supply-chain-attack • https://safedep.io/malicious-durabletask-pypi-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/litellm-compromised-pypi-teampcp-supply-chain-campaign/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpened","FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    FolderPath has "/.aws/","aws",
    FolderPath has "/.azure/","azure",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    FolderPath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    FolderPath has "/.docker/","docker",
    FileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    FileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    FolderPath has "/.config/gh/" and FileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    FolderPath has "/.ssh/" and FileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"/",FileName), 20), Cmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| extend SecretFamily = case(
    TargetFilePath has "/.aws/","aws",
    TargetFilePath has "/.azure/","azure",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gcloud/","gcp",
    TargetFilePath has "/.kube/","k8s",
    TargetFilePath has "/.docker/","docker",
    TargetFileName =~ ".npmrc","npm",
    TargetFileName =~ ".git-credentials","git",
    TargetFilePath has "/.config/gh/" and TargetFileName =~ "hosts.yml","gh",
    TargetFilePath has "/.ssh/" and TargetFileName startswith "id_","ssh",
    "other")
| where SecretFamily != "other"
| summarize DistinctSecretFamilies = dcount(SecretFamily), SecretFamilies = make_set(SecretFamily), PathSample = make_set(TargetFilePath, 20), Cmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where DistinctSecretFamilies >= 3
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:OPENAT OR @auditd.type:PATH) @process.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */python3.*) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.azure/accessTokens.json OR */.azure/azureProfile.json OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db OR */.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json OR */.kube/config OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.git-credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.ssh/id_*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/\/python3?(\.\d+)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.azure\/(accessTokens|azureProfile)\.json|\/\.config\/gcloud\/(credentials\.db|application_default_credentials\.json)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.git-credentials|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\/\.ssh\/id_)/i
| case {
    TargetFileName=/\.aws\// | SecretFamily:="aws";
    TargetFileName=/\.azure\// | SecretFamily:="azure";
    TargetFileName=/gcloud\// | SecretFamily:="gcp";
    TargetFileName=/\.kube\// | SecretFamily:="k8s";
    TargetFileName=/\.docker\// | SecretFamily:="docker";
    TargetFileName=/\.npmrc/ | SecretFamily:="npm";
    TargetFileName=/\.git-credentials|\.config\/gh\// | SecretFamily:="git";
    TargetFileName=/\.ssh\/id_/ | SecretFamily:="ssh";
    *;
  }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=SecretFamily, distinct=true, as=DistinctFamilies), collect([SecretFamily, TargetFileName])])
| DistinctFamilies>=3
CLOUD

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

DeviceProcessEvents

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "7d80b3ef74ad7992b93c31966962612e4e2ceb93e7727cdbd1d2a9af47d44ba8", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "aeaf583e20347bf850e2fabdcd6f4982996ba023f8c2cd56bbd299cfd56516f5", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "877ff2531a63393c4cb9c3c86908b62d9c4fc3db971bc231c48537faae6cb3ec", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Microsoft's durabletask package on PyPi Compromised. Mini Shai Hulud attacks aga
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",

| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or SHA1 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc") or MD5 in~ ("069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["069ac1dc7f7649b76bc72a11ac700f373804bfd81dab7e561157b703999f44ce", "3de04fe2a76262743ed089efa7115f4508619838e77d60b9a1aab8b20d2cc8bf", "85f54c089d78ebfb101454ec934c767065a342a43c9ee1beac8430cdd3b2086f", "c0b094e46842260936d4b97ce63e4539b99a3eae48b736798c700217c52569dc"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/managed.pyz*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/run/docker.sock*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/kubectl*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/dev/null*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/usr/bin/pgmonitor.py*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/timezone*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/localtime*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/etc/systemd/system/pgsql-monitor.service*" OR Filesystem.file_name IN ("__init__.py","__main__.py","roulette.py","timeago.js"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

[LLM] BadIIS C2 IP / domain beacon (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) Command & Control High
Detects any host contacting the published BadIIS command-and-control infrastructure: the two domains used for SEO-fraud orchestration plus the five IPs tied to the demo.pdb variant. Pivots across DNS, network-connection, and proxy telemetry. Rationale: Five IPs and two domains (lee.6686ty.vip, iis.01nmwe.xyz) published in the article. These are operational C2 — any contact is a high-fidelity signal. Cross-validated the campaign infrastructure pattern against Trend Micro's Feb-2025 BadIIS write-up which described similar dual-use C2 (one for SEO redirect targets, one for crawler-cloaking content). Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html • https://gbhackers.com/iis-servers/

[LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) initiating outbound connection to public IP Command & Control Medium
Hunts for IIS application-pool worker processes (w3wp.exe) making outbound connections to the public internet. Legitimate IIS sites typically serve inbound; sustained outbound HTTP/HTTPS from w3wp.exe to non-RFC1918 destinations is the textbook BadIIS beacon shape — the malicious native IIS module pulls cloaked SEO content and reports back from inside the worker process. Rationale: Article-specific because BadIIS is a *native IIS module* loaded into w3wp.exe — every C2 beacon, every cloaked-content fetch, every SEO-redirect lookup flows out as outbound HTTP from the worker process. Elastic and Trend Micro both describe the module reaching a backend for crawler-decision content, confirming the egress pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090 T1505.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt","ConnectionRequest")
| where RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(RemoteIP), SampleUrl=any(RemoteUrl), SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc
let IISHosts = ImProcessCreate

    | summarize by DvcHostname;
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname in (IISHosts) or SrcHostname in (IISHosts)
| where DstPortNumber in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| where DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "127." and DstIpAddr !startswith "169.254."

| summarize ConnCount=count(), DistinctDests=dcount(DstIpAddr), SampleHost=any(DstHostname), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 3
| order by ConnCount desc

[LLM] IIS native module DLL drop or applicationHost.config modification by non-IIS process Installation High
Detects file writes of DLLs into IIS module load paths (System32\inetsrv, Microsoft.NET\Framework64) or modifications to applicationHost.config performed by processes other than the standard IIS / Windows-installer service set. This is the BadIIS persistence install footprint — the malware copies its DLL into a module path then registers it via globalModules. Rationale: Article describes 'service-based installers, droppers, and persistence mechanisms that automate deployment, ensure survivability across IIS server restarts.' External corroboration (Elastic, Trend Micro) confirms BadIIS persistence is exactly this: DLL copied to inetsrv\ or Microsoft.NET\Framework64\ + applicationHost.config edited to register the module. Filtering out TrustedInstaller / msiexec / mscorsvw / appcmd / IIS-setup binaries leaves the BadIIS installer's footprint exposed. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://www.welivesecurity.com/2021/08/06/anatomy-native-iis-malware/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/25/b/chinese-speaking-group-manipulates-seo-with-badiis.html
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has @"\inetsrv\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or (FolderPath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and FileName endswith ".dll")
    or FileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectFile = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
    | where (TargetFilePath has @"\inetsrv\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or (TargetFilePath has @"\Microsoft.NET\Framework\" and TargetFileName endswith ".dll")
        or TargetFileName =~ "applicationHost.config"
    | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","msiexec.exe","mscorsvw.exe","iissetup.exe","appcmd.exe","WindowsAdminCenter.exe","WaAppAgent.exe","WindowsAzureGuestAgent.exe","MsDeploy.exe","ngen.exe","setup.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="FileEvent", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256;
let SuspectProcess = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName =~ "appcmd.exe"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install module","add module","/section:globalModules","/section:modules")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ProcessCreate", DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
union SuspectFile, SuspectProcess
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BadIIS Native Module DLL Drop or applicationHost.config Modification
id: c4d8e2a1-6b9f-4d3e-a872-3f1c4e9b7d22
description: Detects file writes of DLLs into IIS module-load paths or modifications to applicationHost.config by processes outside the standard IIS / Windows-installer set — the persistence footprint of BadIIS (Talos demo.pdb variant).
references:

[LLM] IIS worker (w3wp.exe) writing robots.txt / .php / .js into web root Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects IIS worker process writing or modifying SEO-fraud artifact files (robots.txt, PHP backlink scripts, JavaScript redirectors, hijacked HTML) inside the IIS web-root tree. Legitimate IIS workers serve files; only a malicious in-process module writes content back into wwwroot — the exact SEO-fraud and content-hijacking behaviour the Talos article describes including 'compatible with Baidu browser + hijacking robots.txt' and 'JavaScript redirectors, PHP backlink scripts'. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'compatible with Baidu browser + hijacking robots.txt' as a malware feature folder, plus 'JavaScript redirectors, PHP backlink scripts' as the builder's output. w3wp.exe writing into its own wwwroot is the most article-specific behavioural signal — legitimate web apps almost never have the worker process modify static SEO files. Elastic's BADIIS write-up corroborates the cloaking-content delivery path through w3wp.exe. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/badiis-to-the-bone-new-insights-to-global-seo-poisoning-campaign • https://blog.alphahunt.io/deep-research-badiis-isnt-enough-the-iis-module-http-fingerprints-that-catch-seo-fraud-cloaking/
ATT&CKT1505.004 T1565.001 T1608.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FileName =~ "robots.txt")
    or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\" and (FileName endswith ".php" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".html" or FileName endswith ".htm"))
    or (FolderPath has @"\inetpub\" and FileName =~ "robots.txt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName =~ "w3wp.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","Created","Modified")
| where (TargetFileName =~ "robots.txt")
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\wwwroot\" and (TargetFileName endswith ".php" or TargetFileName endswith ".js" or TargetFileName endswith ".html" or TargetFileName endswith ".htm"))
    or (TargetFilePath has @"\inetpub\" and TargetFileName =~ "robots.txt")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest

| eval delta = _time - prev_time

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write Installation High
Service install with binPath pointing to user-writeable path or LOLBin. Detects via process telemetry (sc.exe create) and registry (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\* writes).
ATT&CKT1543.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "sc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "create"
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
// EventID 4697 is "Service installed" — direct signal, no cmdline-regex needed.
union
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4697
        | where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account = SubjectUserName,
                  Detail = strcat("ServiceName=", ServiceName, " | Image=", ServiceFileName) ),
    ( SecurityEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where EventID == 4688
        | where Account !endswith "$"
        | where NewProcessName endswith "\sc.exe" and CommandLine has "create"
        | where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(\Users\|\AppData\|\ProgramData\|\Temp\)"
        | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account,
                  Detail = strcat("4688 sc.exe create: ", CommandLine) )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Service Persistence via sc.exe with User-Writable Path
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0e
status: experimental
description: |
    sc.exe create with the binary path under \Users\, \AppData\,
    \ProgramData\, or \Temp\ — service-install persistence outside
    legitimate program directories.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1543.003
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_sc:
        Image|endswith: '\sc.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'create'
    selection_path:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\Users\'
            - '\AppData\'
            - '\ProgramData\'
            - '\Temp\'
    condition: selection_sc and selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Internal install scripts dropping a service from %ProgramData%
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
        where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\*"
          AND Registry.registry_value_name="ImagePath"
          AND (Registry.registry_value_data="*\Users\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\AppData\*"
            OR Registry.registry_value_data="*\Temp\*")
        by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="sc.exe" AND Processes.process="*create*"
      AND (Processes.process="*\Users\*" OR Processes.process="*\AppData\*"
        OR Processes.process="*\ProgramData\*" OR Processes.process="*\Temp\*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Mini Shai-Hulud strikes again: npm worm compromises hundreds of @antv packages

Aikido
2026-05-19 14 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm has hit Alibaba's @antv packages, echarts-for-react, and timeago.js. The payload steals CI/CD secrets, plants backdoors in VS Code and Claude Code, and spreads by republishing compromised packages. Here is what happened and how to protect your team. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1027 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003
Domainst.m-kosche.com

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Mini Shai-Hulud strikes again: npm worm compromises hundreds of @antv packages
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload by SHA256 · [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud persistence hooks written into .vscode/ and .claude/ configs · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 exfil to t.m-kosche.com disguised as OpenTelemetry collector · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping via /proc · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 exfil to t.m-kosche.com disguised as OpenTelemetry collector Command & Control High
Hunts outbound connections/DNS to the campaign's fallback C2 t.m-kosche.com, which receives RSA-encrypted stolen credentials over OpenTelemetry-style paths (/api/public/otel/v1/traces) on 443. The domain is unique to this campaign and confirmed by multiple vendors, making any contact high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-unique C2 domain t.m-kosche.com confirmed by StepSecurity, Microsoft, Snyk and JFrog write-ups; the OTel path /api/public/otel/v1/traces detail was added from cross-referenced sources. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-mass-npm-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-antv-ecosystem • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-here-we-go-again-may19/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041

ImDnsActivity

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm payload by SHA256 Installation High
Detects the worm's obfuscated payload file landing or executing on a host by its confirmed SHA256 hashes. High-fidelity exact-match IOC for the AntV-wave payload. Rationale: Uses the two pre-extracted SHA256 payload hashes as exact-match file/process IOCs — zero ambiguity, only ships because the campaign is documented by multiple vendors. [LLM] GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process-memory secret scraping via /proc Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the worm's embedded Python helper that scans /proc for the Runner.Worker process and reads its memory to recover masked CI/CD secrets in plaintext. Targets Linux CI runners where a node/npm-spawned interpreter references Runner.Worker or /proc/<pid>/mem. Rationale: Anchored on the campaign-specific Runner.Worker /proc memory-scraping technique (the novel CI secret-recovery method) corroborated by Microsoft and the Securonix beta analytic; scoped to npm/node-spawned interpreters to cut noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/ • https://connect.securonix.com/threat-research-intelligence-62/beta-detection-mini-shai-hulud-runner-worker-memory-secret-extraction-analytic-308
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/proc/self/mem","process_vm_readv") or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"/proc/[0-9]+/mem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","npm","npx","sh","bash","python","python3")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "Runner.Worker" or SyslogMessage has_any ("/proc/self/mem","process_vm_readv")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("node","npm","python")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud persistence hooks written into .vscode/ and .claude/ configs Installation Medium
Detects node/npm/npx processes writing into .vscode/ or .claude/ configuration directories, where the worm plants auto-execution hooks that survive across sessions and cloned repos. Combination of a JS toolchain process touching these trusted IDE/agent config dirs is the article-specific signal. Rationale: Anchored on the worm's documented persistence in .claude/ and .vscode/ trusted config dirs (Akamai/Microsoft); scopes to the JS toolchain (node/npm/npx) as the writing process to separate from normal IDE activity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/mini-shai-hulud-worm-returns-goes-public • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/20/mini-shai-hulud-compromised-antv-npm-packages-enable-ci-cd-credential-theft/

| where FileName endswith ".json" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".sh"

| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",

      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
