File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm preinstall hook spawning bun runtime Installation High
Detects npm/node spawning the bun JavaScript runtime to execute a root-level index.js — the exact lifecycle pattern the May 2026 AntV supply-chain attack uses to fire 498KB obfuscated payload during npm install of @antv/g6, echarts-for-react, size-sensor, timeago.js and 319 other packages. bun is rarely a legitimate npm child in enterprise CI/dev environments. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim 'preinstall': 'bun run index.js' lifecycle hook combined with the article's named parent context (npm install). Bun-as-child-of-npm has near-zero legitimate baseline in dev/CI fleets outside the Bun ecosystem itself. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","npm.exe","node","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install")
| where FileName in~ ("bun","bun.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "index.js"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\npm.exe","\\node.exe","/npm","/node")
    or CommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/bun"
| where CommandLine has "index.js"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, AccountName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: npm-spawned bun runtime executing index.js (Mini Shai-Hulud AntV)
id: 4f8c1b9e-5d3a-4e7c-9a2f-1b8e7d4c6a31
description: Detects npm/node spawning the bun JavaScript runtime to execute index.js, the preinstall lifecycle loader used by the Mini Shai-Hulud AntV supply-chain compromise (May 2026).
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud Claude Code SessionStart hook injection via npm install Installation High
Detects npm/node/bun writing .claude/settings.json or .claude/setup.mjs, the AI-coding-agent hijack used by the AntV wave to re-execute the credential-harvesting payload every time a developer opens a new Claude Code session in an infected workspace. Legitimate Claude Code settings are authored by the user via the IDE, never by an install lifecycle process. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim persistence path '.claude/settings.json with a SessionStart hook executing node .claude/setup.mjs'. Pairing the file path with an npm-family writer is high-fidelity because Claude Code settings are normally authored by Code.exe / claude CLI itself, never by node during an install. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1546 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.claude\" or FolderPath has "/.claude/")
| where FileName in~ ("settings.json","setup.mjs","settings.local.json")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","bun.exe","npm","node","bun")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] VS Code tasks.json folderOpen persistence written by npm install chain Installation Medium
Detects npm/node/bun writing .vscode/tasks.json, the IDE-folderOpen persistence used by the Mini Shai-Hulud AntV wave so the payload re-executes whenever a developer opens the project workspace in VS Code. Legitimate tasks.json is authored by the IDE itself or committed by humans, not by npm install. Rationale: Anchored on article's '.vscode/tasks.json with runOn:folderOpen' persistence claim. Legitimate tasks.json writes come from Code.exe / human edit; npm-as-writer is the discriminator. Hunting tier because some legitimate npm scaffolders (e.g. create-react-app variants) do write workspace tasks — but in combination with the .claude UC firing on same InitiatingProcessId, confidence escalates. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1546

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" or FolderPath has "/.vscode/")
| where FileName =~ "tasks.json"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","npm","node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","bun.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\.vscode\\tasks.json","/.vscode/tasks.json")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","npx")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud Linux daemon persistence: kitty/cat.py and systemd user service Installation High
Detects creation of ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py or ~/.config/systemd/user/*.service by an npm/node/bun process — the OS-level Linux persistence chain that polls GitHub commit search hourly for 'firedalazer'-keyword commands signed with the attacker's 4096-bit RSA-PSS public key. The cat.py + systemd unit combination is article-specific and has near-zero legitimate baseline. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim '~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py' and 'systemd user service' persistence path. The path is misleading by design (looks like the kitty terminal cache) but kitty itself never writes cat.py. Combined with an npm-family writer, the FP rate is effectively zero. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has "/.local/share/kitty/" and FileName =~ "cat.py")
    or (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and FileName endswith ".service")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","npx","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm","node","bun")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentWriter = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetFilePath has "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user/" and TargetFilePath endswith ".service")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node","bun","yarn","pnpm","sh","bash","dash","zsh")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud C2 backchannel: python polling GitHub commit search for 'firedalazer' Command & Control High
Detects Python processes reaching api.github.com/search/commits with the 'firedalazer' keyword — the C2 backchannel used by the kitty/cat.py daemon to fetch RSA-PSS-signed command payloads. Hourly poll cadence and the specific search keyword make this article-grade high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim 'polls the GitHub commit search API hourly for commands containing the keyword firedalazer'. The hourly poll cadence (PollCount >= 4 over 7d window catches the daemon while avoiding a one-off curl), python initiator with cat.py in the cmdline, and the unique 'firedalazer' keyword all combine to article-grade fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1102.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python.exe","python3","python3.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py",".local/share/kitty","kitty\\cat.py","firedalazer")
| summarize PollCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP
| where PollCount >= 4
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationHostName =~ "api.github.com" or RequestURL has "api.github.com"
| where RequestURL has "/search/commits" or RequestURL has "firedalazer"
| where RequestClientApplication startswith "python-requests"
| summarize PollCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleUrls = make_set(RequestURL, 5)
          by SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestClientApplication
| where PollCount >= 4
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR */python OR */python3) @DestinationHostname:api.github.com @CommandLine:(*cat.py* OR *kitty* OR *firedalazer*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^api\.github\.com$/i ContextImageFileName=/python(3)?(\.exe)?$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/(cat\.py|kitty[\\\/]cat\.py|\.local[\\\/]share[\\\/]kitty|firedalazer)/i}, field=ContextProcessId, key=TargetProcessId, include=[CommandLine])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| _count >= 4
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest="api.github.com" AND (Web.url="*search/commits*" OR Web.url="*firedalazer*") AND (Web.http_user_agent="python-requests*") by host, src, src_user, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | stats count min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime dc(url) as distinct_urls values(http_user_agent) as ua by host, src, src_user | where count >= 4
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest="api.github.com" AND (Web.url="*search/commits*" OR Web.url="*firedalazer*") AND (Web.http_user_agent="python-requests*") by host, src, src_user, Web.url, Web.http_method, Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | stats count min(firstTime) as firstTime max(lastTime) as lastTime dc(url) as distinct_urls values(http_user_agent) as ua by host, src, src_user | where count >= 4
[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud GitHub dead-drop exfiltration via python-requests/2.31.0 Actions on Objectives High
Detects POST/PUT to api.github.com from a python-requests/2.31.0 User-Agent creating Dune-themed repositories or committing 'results-<timestamp>-<counter>.json' files. This is the article's secondary exfil channel activated when the malware harvests a developer's GitHub PAT, used to stash AES-256-GCM-encrypted credential dumps. Rationale: Anchored on the article's three concrete IOCs: User-Agent string 'python-requests/2.31.0', the exfil filename pattern 'results/results-<timestamp>-<counter>.json', and the Dune-themed repo naming convention (sardaukar/fremen/atreides + sandworm/ornithopter/stillsuit). Triple-anchor (UA + method + path keyword) keeps FP rate well below a generic python-requests-to-github hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1567 T1102.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let SuspiciousPython = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3.exe","python3")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cat.py",".local/share/kitty","kitty\\cat.py")
    | project DeviceId, ProcessId, PyStart=Timestamp, PyCmd=ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "api.github.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3.exe","python3")
| join kind=inner SuspiciousPython on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ProcessId
| summarize Connections = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleUrls = make_set(RemoteUrl, 5), SampleCmd = any(PyCmd)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationHostName =~ "api.github.com"
| where RequestClientApplication startswith "python-requests/2.31"
| where RequestMethod in ("POST","PUT","PATCH")
| where RequestURL has_any ("/user/repos","/contents/results-","sardaukar","fremen","atreides","sandworm","ornithopter","stillsuit","harkonnen")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, SentBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

            - 'wget '

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or SHA1 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446") or MD5 in~ ("a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a68dd1e6a6e35ec3771e1f94fe796f55dfe65a2b94560516ff4ac189390dfa1c", "fb5c97557230a27460fdab01fafcfabeaa49590bafd5b6ef30501aa9e0a51142", "783b4019fc5b942a29846132d28441c8fc31bed8", "b06b126b9e26af03a7ef2f8b8e90d446"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Outbound egress to node-ipc stealer infrastructure (azurestaticprovider[.]net / 37.16.75.69) Actions on Objectives High
Detects network connections to attacker-owned exfiltration infrastructure used by the malicious node-ipc 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 npm packages published 14 May 2026. Any host reaching these atoms after package install should be treated as a credential-theft incident. Rationale: Pivots on two atomic IOCs explicitly named in the Snyk advisory (37.16.75.69 and azurestaticprovider.net), each independently corroborated by StepSecurity and Upwind. No expected legitimate traffic to either atom — attacker-owned exfil infrastructure. [LLM] DNS lookup for azurestaticprovider[.]net node-ipc exfil domain Command & Control High
Surfaces hosts resolving the attacker-controlled domain azurestaticprovider.net (or sh.azurestaticprovider.net) used by the malicious node-ipc payload, even when the subsequent TCP egress is firewall-blocked. DNS-layer pivot catches hosts that loaded the package but did not complete exfiltration. Rationale: DNS pivot catches the same campaign at an earlier layer than TCP egress and survives proxy-level blocks. Domain is unique to this campaign and referenced verbatim in StepSecurity, Upwind, and Snyk advisories. ContextImageFileName lets the analyst confirm node.exe / npm as the requesting process. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "azurestaticprovider.net"
   or RemoteUrl endswith ".azurestaticprovider.net"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Hits=count(),
            SampleProc=any(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            SampleCmd=any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
            SampleUser=any(InitiatingProcessAccountName)
            by DeviceName, RemoteUrl
| order by FirstSeen asc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Name has "azurestaticprovider.net"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DnsQuery has "azurestaticprovider.net"
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DnsResponseCodeName, EventProduct)
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] node-ipc stealer __ntw=1 environment marker in process command line Installation High
Hunts for the __ntw=1 environment-variable marker reportedly used by the malicious node-ipc payload to signal that a child has already inherited the stealer context (preventing re-entry). Presence of this token in any process or child command-line is a high-fidelity indicator the payload executed on the host. Rationale: `__ntw=1` is a campaign-specific environment marker called out verbatim in the Snyk advisory and corroborated by StepSecurity — no mainstream npm package or build tool uses this token. Single-string match on CommandLine works because env vars set inline (e.g. `__ntw=1 node ...`) and parent-spawned children with that prefix surface in EDR command-line telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1027 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
    or ParentProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "__ntw=1"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessCommandLine, EventProduct),
(SecurityEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where EventID == 4688
 | where CommandLine has "__ntw=1" or ParentProcessName has "__ntw=1"
 | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hunts for file-system writes of node-ipc.cjs into any node_modules/node-ipc/ directory after the 14 May 2026 publication window, surfacing developer workstations, CI runners, build containers, and artifact registries that installed a candidate-malicious release. Pair with version triage (9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1). Rationale: Anchors on the exact CommonJS file Snyk identifies as malicious (`node-ipc.cjs`) and the canonical install path (`node_modules/node-ipc/`). Time-bound to the publication window so analysts only see installs that could be the bad versions. Hunting tier because a hit alone does not prove the version is malicious — needs package.json/lockfile triage as Step 1. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/stealer-backdoor-found-in-3-node-ipc.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp >= datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules" and FolderPath has "node-ipc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated >= datetime(2026-05-14T00:00:00Z)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| where TargetFileName =~ "node-ipc.cjs"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules" and TargetFilePath has "node-ipc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated asc

[LLM] node.js process staging credential dump in nt-* temp directory Actions on Objectives Medium
Detects the staging artefact the malicious node-ipc payload writes — a temp directory matching `$TMPDIR/nt-*` populated by a node process — used to compress harvested SSH / cloud / kube / GitHub / Terraform / shell-history credentials before exfil. Catches the campaign at the collection layer even if egress is firewall-blocked. Rationale: Combines two campaign-specific behaviours from the Snyk advisory: (a) the temp directory prefix `nt-` and (b) a node process as the writer. Threshold of ≥3 distinct files per directory suppresses single-file noise while still firing on the credential-dump fan-out (90+ categories). Catches the campaign at the collection step even when egress is blocked. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.upwind.io/feed/malicious-node-ipc-npm-package-credential-theft
ATT&CKT1074.001 T1552.001 T1560.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)([\\/]Temp[\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp),
            DistinctFiles=dcount(FileName), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 25),
            TotalBytes=sum(FileSize)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FolderPath
| where DistinctFiles >= 3
| order by FirstSeen asc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)([\\/]Temp[\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)"
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctFiles=dcount(TargetFileName),
            SampleFiles=make_set(TargetFileName, 25), TotalBytes=sum(TargetFileSize)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, EventProduct
| where DistinctFiles >= 3
| order by FirstSeen asc
title: Node.js Process Writes to nt-* Temp Directory (node-ipc Stealer Staging)
id: f0c5e842-9a16-4a3d-b71e-2c0d8e5fa317
description: Detects a Node.js process creating files in a temp directory matching the nt-* prefix reportedly used by the malicious node-ipc 9.1.6 / 9.2.3 / 12.0.1 payload to stage harvested credentials before exfiltration.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/malicious-node-ipc-versions-published-npm/
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/node-ipc-npm-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/19
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1074.001
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Temp\nt-'
      - '/tmp/nt-'
      - '/T/nt-'
  condition: selection_image and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Node.js tooling that happens to use an nt- prefix for scratch files (rare)
level: medium

(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) (@TargetFilename:*\\Temp\\nt-* OR @TargetFilename:*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\nt-*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @process.name:node (@file.path:/tmp/nt-* OR @file.path:/var/folders/*/T/nt-*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/[\\\\/]node(\\.exe)?$/i
| regex("([\\\\/]Temp[\\\\/]nt-|/tmp/nt-|/var/folders/.+?/T/nt-)", field=TargetFileName, flags=i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function={
    distinct_count := count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true)
  })
| distinct_count >= 3
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as file_count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/folders/*/T/nt-*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where file_count >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_name) as files dc(Filesystem.file_name) as file_count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Temp\\nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/tmp/nt-*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/var/folders/*/T/nt-*") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where file_count >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The time of much patching is coming
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
[LLM] Talos weekly top-prevalent malware hash watch (Coinminer / Injector / W32.Variant) Installation High
Surfaces any execution, image-load, or file-write of the four SHA256/MD5 hashes Cisco Talos published in the 2026-05-14 Threat Source newsletter as the most prevalent malware seen in Talos telemetry that week (Win.Worm.Coinminer VID001.exe, W32.Injector d4aa3e70…_63_Exe.exe, W32.Variant u112417.dat, Auto.90B145 APQ9305.dll). Article-specific because it pins on the exact SHA256/MD5 + Talos detection names from this week's bulletin, not a generic IOC sweep. Rationale: Hash IOCs are deterministic — these four SHA256s and the four MD5s come straight from Cisco Talos's weekly telemetry top-list with named verdicts (Win.Worm.Coinminer::1201, W32.Injector:Gen.21ie.1201, W32.Variant:MalwareXgenMisc.29d4.1201, Auto.90B145.282358.in02). They were corroborated by following each Talos file-reputation URL embedded in the article (talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=<SHA256>) which is Talos's authoritative reputation service confirming the verdict. The example filenames VID001.exe / u112417.dat / APQ9305.dll are renameable and only used as soft secondary signal in Splunk — the SHA256/MD5 are the high-fidelity anchors. FP rate is low because we're hash-pinned; the only realistic FPs are authorized malware sandbox hosts (allowlist them). Cross-checked against: • https://blog.talosintelligence.com/the-time-of-much-patching-is-coming/ • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974 • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba • https://talosintelligence.com/talos_file_reputation?s=90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1496 T1055 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let MaliciousSHA256 = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba","90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59"]);
let MaliciousMD5 = dynamic(["2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba","c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
let KnownFilenames = dynamic(["VID001.exe","u112417.dat","APQ9305.dll"]);
union
  ( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256)
        or MD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
        or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256)
        or InitiatingProcessMD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
    | extend SourceTable = "DeviceProcessEvents"
    | project Timestamp, SourceTable, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
  ( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256) or MD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
    | extend SourceTable = "DeviceFileEvents"
    | project Timestamp, SourceTable, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
  ( DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256) or MD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
    | extend SourceTable = "DeviceImageLoadEvents"
    | project Timestamp, SourceTable, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousSHA256 = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507","96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974","e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba","90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59"]);
let MaliciousMD5 = dynamic(["2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f","aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9","dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba","c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
  ( ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256) or MD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
    | extend SourceTable = "ImProcessCreate"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine ),
  ( ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where TargetFileSHA256 in (MaliciousSHA256) or TargetFileMD5 in (MaliciousMD5)
    | extend SourceTable = "ImFileEvent"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceTable, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution

references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:

    - attack.credential-access

    category: process_access
    product: windows

        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:

            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same

references:

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or SHA1 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a") or MD5 in~ ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.file_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name, Filesystem.file_hash
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.process_hash IN ("9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507", "96fa6a7714670823c83099ea01d24d6d3ae8fef027f01a4ddac14f123b1c9974", "e60ab99da105ee27ee09ea64ed8eb46d8edc92ee37f039dbc3e2bb9f587a33ba", "90b1456cdbe6bc2779ea0b4736ed9a998a71ae37390331b6ba87e389a49d3d59", "2915b3f8b703eb744fc54c81f4a9c67f", "aac3165ece2959f39ff98334618d10d9", "dbd8dbecaa80795c135137d69921fdba", "c2efb2dcacba6d3ccc175b6ce1b7ed0a")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process_hash
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
